title: Sparse density mode, contextual column affordances, and privacy-friendly row obfuscation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: Design and prototype a new ‘sparse’ density mode and complementary column affordances for the virtualized table component. Include an optional privacy-friendly row obfuscation mode for shared/example data. This ticket covers UX patterns, interaction specs, accessibility notes, and handoff artifacts for engineering. The sparse density mode should prioritize scanability for extremely long tables (thousands+ rows) by increasing row-collapse heuristics, reducing padding, and introducing contextual reveal affordances for dense cells. Column affordances include a subtle hover rail for resize, a soft-snap grid when dragging, and a multi-select header for bulk column actions (hide/pin/lock). Privacy-friendly obfuscation is an optional toggle at the table level that replaces sensitive cell content with low-fidelity placeholders and unobtrusive masks, while retaining sort/filter behavior and keyboard navigation for power users.
acceptance_criteria: Sparse density is represented in the component token set and can be toggled by a prop (density: 'sparse')
Resize affordance visual spec: hover rail (6px) appears on column hover; drag snaps to 8px increments; final width announced via aria-live
Privacy obfuscation toggles mask text but preserves value metadata used for sorting/filtering and for copy-on-click when permitted
Virtualization behavior: no layout jank for 95% of user interactions; reflow <40ms on M1-class machine when switching density or toggling obfuscation
Accessibility: screen reader announces density changes and column resize completion; keyboard-first users can resize with modifier + arrow keys
Design tokens: spacing, typography, and skeleton opacity variables included for sparse density and obfuscation state
Figma prototype linked and validated in research sessions with 4 engineers and 2 PMs
design_notes: Sparse density differs from compact: instead of only reducing vertical padding, it collapses secondary metadata and defers non-critical actions to contextual menus. Cells with long text render a single-line ellipsis with a reveal affordance on hover or focus.

Introduce a 'soft-resize' interaction: while dragging, column content scales using a lightweight CSS transform to avoid full layout invalidation. On drop, we apply the final width to the layout and animate opacity to mask snapping artifacts.

For privacy obfuscation, we use three states: masked (shimmer block), blurred (low-contrast glyphs), and tokenized (first/last char visible). Default is masked. The sensitive-field list is managed via column metadata passed by devs.

Virtualization: prototype uses variable-height buffering (river-buffer) to better handle occasional taller rows without overallocating DOM nodes. This ties into the sparse mode because collapsed cells are variable height until expanded.

Sorting & filtering UX: inline filter chips live in header row; an 'open filter' keyboard shortcut focuses first filter control. Filters remain functional while obfuscation is on — comparisons operate on the underlying value, not the masked label.

Performance trade-offs: soft-resize improves perceived latency at the expense of a small extra paint on drop. River-buffer reduces DOM churn but increases bookkeeping complexity; engineering review required to ensure memory budget remains under 5%.

Design tokens to add: --table-density-sparse-row-padding, --table-sparse-secondary-opacity, --table-obfuscation-shimmer-opacity, --table-resize-snap-grid. These should live in tokens/tables and map to existing density scale.
We should not auto-collapse actionable cells (buttons, anchors) in sparse mode — instead show an affordance that expands the row inline.
Edge case: pinned/frozen columns must ignore river-buffer height compensation and always render in stable layout to avoid visual mismatch when expanding rows.

decisions: Adopt sparse density as separate tokenized mode (do not overload 'compact')
Use soft-resize transforms to mask layout thrash, fallback to standard resize if transform not supported
Privacy obfuscation is opt-in per-table and controlled by column metadata; data for sorting/filtering remains in the DOM but hidden from visual output
River-buffer virtualization will be the primary approach for variable row heights; we will provide a plain-window fallback for older browsers
